### Who Me?! Jealous?
Author: Jeff Schreve
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/fromhisheart/from-his-heart-week-of-april-24-11602713.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 18:8
Points:
- Jealousy is a destructive heart issue that personal pride makes people reluctant to acknowledge.
- Saul allowed the celebratory song praising David to ignite bitter envy and resentment.
- Constantly comparing oneself to others produces either arrogant pride or deep discouragement.
- Believers are called to focus on doing their best with what God provided rather than trying to be the best.
- Keeping your focus on pleasing God protects the heart from competitive bitterness.

### Preparing for Opposition
Author: Jack Graham
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/powerpoint/powerpoint-july-16-2010-11634823.html
Passage: 1 Samuel 18:8-9
Points:
- Experiencing victory and blessing often attracts unexpected opposition and envy.
- Saul viewed David's triumph as a personal loss, giving root to jealousy and suspicion.
- Entertaining envy caused Saul to lose spiritual peace and fall under God's discipline.
- Envy and pushback can arise even from within the community of God's people.
- Believers should stay focused on praising God and trust Him to handle their critics.
